title: Jamo Monument — AG Publication Poster
description: A single Hangul word scaled to architectural dominance, its jamo components revealed through cobalt construction-line overlays. Channels Ahn Sang-soo's structural philosophy and Workroom Press's spare editorial precision.
philosophy: This template treats Hangul not as language but as geometric sculpture — each jamo a cell in a visible grid, each stroke a traced argument about form. It rejects decorative backgrounds, narrative imagery, and crowded layouts in favour of one word carrying the full visual weight of a slide. The speaker is a type educator, cultural institution, or design studio with something deliberate to say about the letterform itself. It belongs in symposia, graduate critiques, and publishing-house presentations where the silence around a subject matters as much as the subject.
goodFor: Typography lectures and Korean type-history symposia
Section-break or title slides anchored by a single concept word
Book launch and editorial identity reveals
avoidFor: Multi-bullet corporate training or compliance decks
Presentations requiring dense Latin-script body text columns
Sales pitches needing warm, approachable visual language
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a wall-scale monument in an empty gallery — one Hangul word commands the entire field, its jamo anatomy exposed through hairline construction overlays that read as both analysis and reverence. Mood is Spartan and architectural: a structural diagram, not a decorative poster, shaped by editorial restraint and the charged silence of deliberate negative space. Avoid illustrative texture, gradient wash, or any secondary imagery competing with the letterform's geometric authority.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with the hero Hangul word spanning cols 1–12 at near-edge-to-edge bleed, vertically centered with a tight 4% top-and-bottom margin to let the form breathe against raw field. Cobalt construction-line overlays subdivide each jamo cell, tracing stroke anatomy across the full composition as a visible structural argument. Deck identity — presentation title and institution name — locks to the bottom-left corner in a compact two-line block occupying cols 1–4, hierarchy achieved through size contrast alone. No header band, no page number, no decorative frame on this slide.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a page from a rigorous typographic monograph — clinical, deliberate, and quietly reverent. A monumental jamo anchors the field as pure geometric sculpture, its construction-line skeleton laid bare as argument rather than ornament, while a lean annotation column on the far right carries the sole verbal weight. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric and taut: monolith on the left, a whispered counter-voice on the right. Avoid any illustrative texture, gradient wash, or decorative device that competes with the letterform's structural authority.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid: a single jamo or short Hangul concept word dominates cols 1–8 at near-bleed scale, its structural cells exposed by hairline construction-line overlays spanning the full field. Cols 9–12 hold a flush-right annotation block — a short quote, working definition, or attribution stacked vertically — separated from the type field by a single vertical rule. No header band; a folio and section tag are pinned bottom-right, outside the rule line. Outer margins breathe at roughly 6–7% so the letterform reads as architecturally self-sufficient.
